issues: No integrity concerns: the change only applies log1p to the training target and expm1 to the predictions. It reads no files and uses no test labels.

Recomputed z of about 2.40 (candidate mean 0.57205 vs incumbent 0.5926, diff 0.02055, SE = 0.007*sqrt(1/2+1/1) = 0.00857) is close to the reported 2.383. The small gap is probably due to the exact sd or rounding of the adjusted values.
The incumbent mean rests on a single run, so its noise carries fully into the comparison. Both candidate runs still beat it by at least 0.018.

expm1 preserves rank order and the loss is Spearman-based, so the back-transform can't change the score. log1p assumes targets above -1; clearance values are non-negative and both runs finished, so this holds.

issues: No sign of getting around the measurement. The diff only swaps the RandomForestRegressor for an XGBRegressor. It reads no files, pastes in no answers and never uses the test labels. Only train_y is used for fitting.

No bug that would make the result meaningless. The seed is passed as random_state. With subsample=0.8, the XGBoost randomness depends on that seed. The log1p target transform is unchanged. Spearman depends only on rank order, so it does not matter whether predictions are converted back from the log scale.

Recomputed z: the candidate mean is (0.5583+0.5631)/2 = 0.5607, and the incumbent mean is 0.5720, so the gain is 0.0113. The standard error is sqrt(0.0070^2/2 + 0.0070^2/2) = 0.0070, giving z ≈ 1.61. This matches the harness value of 1.611.
The accept is borderline. A z of 1.61 is moderate evidence from only 2 runs on each side. The gain is about 1.6 noise sd. A replicate run would make it firmer if the budget allows.

Minor style points: MAX_FEATURES now stands for colsample_bytree, which no longer matches its name. The constructor lines have trailing whitespace and odd indentation. The XGBoost settings (depth 6, learning rate 0.1, 300 trees) were not tuned. None of this affects validity.

description: Replace RandomForestRegressor with XGBRegressor to potentially improve performance on high-cardinality fingerprint data.
Replace XGBRegressor with LGBMRegressor from the lightgbm library.

issues: No sign of getting around the measurement. The only change adds TPSA, an RDKit descriptor computed from each molecule's structure. It reads no files, pastes in no answers and uses no test labels.
My recomputed z is about 2.46: (0.5607 - 0.5396) / (0.0070 * sqrt(1/1 + 1/2)) = 0.0211 / 0.00857. That matches the harness's 2.454 apart from rounding of the noise sd.

Only one candidate run supports this. A 0.021 gain from adding a single descriptor is large compared with the noise sd of 0.0070, so luck may account for part of it. Consider one replicate before treating the gain as settled.

Possible bug, already in the incumbent and not added by this diff: the featurizer skips molecules RDKit cannot parse ('if mol is None: continue'). That would shift the feature rows out of line with train_y, or return fewer predictions than test molecules. It does not matter if every SMILES parses, but it is safer to put in a placeholder row than to skip.
